topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the final lecture of the course and outlines the key learning objectives regarding cancer therapy approaches.

topics.label: Conventional cancer therapies: surgery, radiotherapy, and cytotoxic chemotherapy
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe traditional treatment modalities that physically excise tumor mass or non-specifically destroy rapidly dividing cells, alongside their associated toxicities and resistance mechanisms.

topics.label: Targeting intrinsic cancer cell vulnerabilities and DNA repair defects
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain therapeutic approaches designed to exploit specific biological weaknesses in cancer cells, including hormone dependency, checkpoint deficiencies, and defective DNA repair pathways.

topics.label: Oncogene addiction, kinase inhibitors, and therapeutic resistance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics focus on small-molecule inhibitors targeting hyperactivated oncogenic kinases and examine the molecular mechanisms driving drug resistance and tumor adaptation.

topics.label: Monoclonal antibody therapies and antibody-drug conjugates
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss the application of engineered antibodies to target tumor cell-surface antigens directly or to deliver cytotoxic payloads selectively.

topics.label: Cancer immunotherapy: checkpoint blockade, neoantigens, and engineered T-cell therapies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics address the role of the immune system in cancer surveillance and detail modern strategies to reactivate or genetically engineer T cells to eradicate tumors.

topics.label: Challenges, historical progress, and future directions in cancer treatment
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate ongoing systemic hurdles in oncology, historical improvements in patient survival, and future clinical paradigms.
